tiers: 1. Cloudfeet: You may hover 1 foot off the ground, but may not move horizontally while doing so. This grants you immunity to fall damage.
2. Silvered Camouflage: While inside fog, mist, or smoke, you gain an expertise die on Stealth checks.
3. Rolling Mist: You can cast Fog Cloud once per short rest for free. As a free action on each of your turns, you can move the centre of your Fog Clouds up to 30 feet.

4. Eye of the Storm: While outdoors, you gain 50% resistance to cold damage and can breathe normally in any mist, fog, or smoke. Additionally, attacks that can frighten have advantage against creatures of your choice within your Fog Clouds.
5. Windborne Hover: Your Cloudfeet hover height increases to 3 feet, and you can move horizontally at half your speed while hovering. You ignore difficult terrain while doing so.

6. Cloudstride: Mist, fog, and clouds become solid underfoot. You can move across and through them, both horizontally and vertically (stepping through them like stairs) and may end your movement standing upon them, as if they were firm ground.

7. Deepening Veil: Rolling Mist can now be used once per minute (or refreshing upon rolling initiative). Additionally, creatures of your choice that start their turns within your Fog Clouds are sluggish until the start of their next turn.
8. Cloudborne Flow: While moving through mist, fog, and clouds, you can move at half speed through the spaces of foes, and you do not provoke opportunity attacks.

9. Tempest Manifest: Once per long rest, upon rolling for initiative, you can shapeshift into a roaring storm cloud for the remainder of combat. In this form, you gain 60' of fly speed, always count as being within a cloud, and gain immunity to physical damage. Additionally, you project a 10' persistent zone from you that causes 1d8 lightning harm to foes.
10. Sovereign of Clouds: You gain immunity to lightning and thunder damage, and allies within 30' of you gain 50% resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

theme: drawing power from the ethereal plane
tiers: 1. Ethereal Glimmer: You gain advantage on Perception checks made in dim light or darkness. Additionally, you can perceive creatures and objects on the Ethereal Plane within 5 feet of you as faint, translucent outlines.
2. Spectral Footfalls: You gain advantage on Stealth checks while in dim light or darkness.
3. Planar Step: You can cast Misty Step once per short rest for free.
4. Phantom Sense: You can see invisible creatures and objects within 10 feet of you, though they appear as indistinct, wavering shapes.
5. Ghostly Strike: Your damaging attacks deal 1d4 additional force damage as ethereal energy lashes from them.

6. Phantom Form: You can move at half speed through foes and objects. If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and suffer force harm equal to double your level.
7. Spectral Shroud: You gain 50% resistance to physical damage.
8. Ethereal Reach: Your attacks ignore half and three-quarters cover.
9. Ethereal Sovereignty: You gain 60' of truesight and immunity to physical damage. While you are conscious, creatures have disadvantage on armour attack rolls against you.

10. Ethereal Ascendance: You cease to age and gain immunity to disease, poison damage, poison harm, and the poisoned condition. Additionally, once per long rest, when you are reduced to 0 HP, you may choose to automatically succeed your death save and instantly shift to the Ethereal Plane for 1 minute, returning to the Material Plane afterwards with 1 HP.

1. Essence Loom: Once per short rest, you can use an action to create a mundane object of your choice (anything you could purchase from a general adventuring store) made of your essence. The object lasts until destroyed, you dismiss it as a free action, or you use this power again. Objects created with this power have no retail value.
2. Essence Mending: Your Essence Loom objects last until you complete a long rest instead of until your next use of the power. Additionally, you can cast the Mending cantrip at-will.
3. Echoed Toolkit: You can now create tools with your Essence Loom. These tools can be used for one relevant skill check, adding an expertise die to the check.
4. Essence Echo: Whenever you create an object with Essence Loom, you may also create a temporary duplicate. The duplicate exists for 1 minute before vanishing.

5. Soulforged Armament: As an action, you can create a weapon that grants its wielder +1 AB and damage with weapon attacks, or a shield that grants its wielder +1 armour, made of pure essence. The item lasts until you dismiss it as a free action or you create a new one.
6. Essence Fauna: Once per long rest, you can cast Conjure Woodland Beings for free. The creatures summoned appear as translucent, ephemeral creatures woven from your life force.
7. Soulbound Resonance: Your Soulforged Armament's bonuses increase to +2.

8. Essence Companion: Once per long rest, as an action, you can create an Essence Homunculus, a CR 1/4 construct minion that deals force damage. It requires your concentration, but your concentration on it cannot be broken against your will.
9. Soulforged Masterwork: Your Soulforged Armament's bonuses increase to +3. Additionally, you can now have two Soulforged Armaments active at once.
10. Essence Artifice: Upon gaining this tier, you immediately gain 3 white (colour tier 5) loot rolls.
1. Residual Static: You gain an expertise die on finesse checks. Additionally, while moving you shed 5' of bright light as blue sparks flicker over your skin.
2. Magnetic Cling: You gain advantage on Athletics and Brawn checks made to hold onto or climb metal objects and structures.
3. Shocking Palm: You can cast the Shocking Grasp cantrip at will, governing it with any ability.
4. Lightning Ward: You gain 50% resistance to lightning damage.
5. Conductive Strike: You deal 1d4 additional lightning damage with melee attacks.
6. Thunderlash Reflection: Whenever an adjacent creature hits you with an armour attack, it suffers thunder harm equal to your proficiency bonus.
7. Storm Conduit: Whenever you roll lightning or thunder damage dice, you can reroll 1 results once.
8. Static Field: Whenever your turn ends, adjacent foes suffer lightning harm equal to half your proficiency bonus.
9. Storm's Zenith: Your Storm Conduit now changes 1 results into the die's maximum result instead of rerolling them.

10. Electromagnetic Maelstrom: Once per long rest, upon rolling for initiative, you can shapeshift into a whirling storm of electromagnetism for the remainder of combat. In this form, you gain fly speed equal to your Speed, gain immunity to lightning and thunder damage, and can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, taking 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside an object. Additionally, you project a 15' persistent zone from you that causes 2d8 lightning and thunder harm to foes.
1. Squared Stance: Whenever you would be moved against your will or knocked prone by a fortitude or reflex attack while you are standing on the ground, make a save, ignoring the effect on a success.

2. Flattened Slip: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can shapeshift into a 2-foot cube until you revert as a free action. While shapeshifted in this way, you gain advantage on Stealth checks to hide in tight or narrow spaces. You cannot make attacks, use maneuvers, or cast spells while in this form.
3. Edges of Impact: Whenever a creature hits you with a melee armour attack while you are standing on the ground it suffers 1d6 bludgeoning harm from your jarring angular rebound.
4. Hardened Corners: Your angular points thicken with resilient cartilage, granting you +1 armour vs melee attacks.

5. Cube Form: Once per short rest, upon rolling for intiative, you can shapeshift into a cube of size based on your size category for the remainder of combat. In this form, you gain 2 armour and advantage on Strength checks. Additionally, Fortitude attacks against you have disadvantage.
6. Rolling Assault: While in Cube Form, you can use a free action once per round to propel yourself in a straight line up to 30 feet. If you collide with a creature, it suffers 2d8 bludgeoning harm.
7. Facet Expansion: Whenever you shapeshift into your Cube Form, you can choose to become a cube one size larger. If you do so, Rolling Assault's damage is doubled.
8. Robust Facet: Your Rolling Assault's bludgeoning harm increases to 3d8.
9. Quantum Cuboid: Once per long rest while in Cube Form, when you would be hit by an attack, you can shift 5' to reduce the attack's success tier by 1.
10. Transcendent Cube: While in your Cube Form, your Speed is replaced with 60' of teleportation. Your line of sight for this teleportation ignores three quarters cover.
1. Silken Strand: As a bonus action, you can conjure a 5-foot length of silken fiber. It can be used as rope.
2. Resilient Weave: Whenever you complete a rest, a thin, silken cocoon extends over your body, granting you temporary hit points equal to your level.
3. Protective Cocoon: Once per short rest, when you or a creature within 10' of you is targeted by an armour attack, you can reduce the attack's success tier by 1.

4. Ethereal Fibres: Whenever you use Protective Cocoon, the target also gains 50% resistance to your choice of one of the triggering attack's base damage types for 1 round. Additionally, you can now use Protective Cocoon twice per short rest.

5. Hardened Chrysalis: Protective Cocoon also reduces the success tiers of other incoming armour attacks for 1 round, and whenever the cocooned creature would be frightened or charmed, they make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
6. Regenerative Shell: At the end of each of your turns in combat, all creatures inside any of your cocoons heal hit points equal to 1d8 + your proficiency bonus.

7. Living Cocoon: Once per long rest, as a free action, you envelop an adjacent willing creature within a translucent cocoon. The creature gains total cover from outside the cocoon. The cocoon lasts for 1 round, and any healing received from Regenerative Shell is doubled in it.
8. Metamorphic Enclosure: When your Living Cocoon ends, the freed creature chooses one: immediately shift up to half its speed, or gain advantage on its next attack.

9. Transcendant Shroud: Creatures inside your Living Cocoon that are healed by Regenerative Shell are immediately cured of any diseases or poisons. Additionally, you can now use Living Cocoon twice per long rest.

10. Cocoon of the First Dawn: Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes creating a 30'x30' cocoon. All creatures inside the cocoon when it is created are healed for a total of 100 hit points that you can allocate freely, are cured of one condition each, and for the next hour, count as being inside one of your cocoons and reduce the success tier of all incoming armour attacks by 1. After being created and granting its effects instantaneously to the creatures inside it, the cocoon is destroyed.

1. Vacuum Edge: As an action, you can call into your main hand a knife with a blade comprised of a vacuum, so long as you aren't wielding anything else there. The Vacuum Edge is a martial melee weapon of the knife category that you have proficiency in. It deals 1d4 + STR/DEX force damage and has the Fatal and Thrown (20'/60') traits. Additionally, you have +1 weapon AB while wielding it.
2. Anti-Flame Siphon: Whenever you hit with your Vacuum Edge, all non-magical flames adjacent to the target are extinguished as the area is briefly robbed of oxygen.
3. Absolute Emptiness: Whenever you score a killing blow with your Vacuum Edge, the target disintegrates into nothingness. Its soul does not pass to the afterlife.
4. Void Resonance: Whenever you score a critical success with your Vacuum Edge, the target makes a save, becoming debilitated for 1 round on a fail.
5. Kinetic Reach: While wielding your Vacuum Edge, your weapon reach increases by 5'.
6. Silent Slice: Attacking with your Vacuum Edge doesn't reveal you while you are hidden, except to the creature you attacked.
7. Pressure Deepening: Whenever you hit the same creature with Vacuum Edge for 3 of your turns in a row, the 3rd hit deals 2d6 additional force damage.
8. Siphoning Slash: Whenever you hit with your Vacuum Edge, you heal hit points equal to half the damage dealt (rounded up).
9. Inexorable Pull: Your fortitude, reflex, and will attacks have advantage against creatures within 10' of you while you are wielding your Vacuum Edge.

10. Singularity Slash: Once per long rest, as a free action while wielding your Vacuum Edge, you can form a 60' line of nothingness, causing 7d8 force harm to all creatures within it. Creatures killed by this harm count as being killed by your Vacuum Edge.
1. Quick-Mix Instincts: Your first melee attack of each combat deals 1d4 additional poison damage.
2. Minor Tincture Infusion: Your melee attacks deal 1d4 additional acid damage.

3. Potent Catalyst: Your Minor Tincture Infusion dice are increased to d6s. Additionally, whenever you score a critical success with a melee attack, the target suffers acid harm at the start of its next turn equal to your proficiency bonus.
4. Volatile Throw: As a free action, you can throw an alchemical bomb up to 30', which explodes in a 5' radius. All creatures within the area suffer 1d4 acid harm.
5. Combustion: Your Volatile Throw bombs now cause acid and fire harm.

6. Viscous Countermeasure: The first time each round you are hit by an adjacent creature, you can coat yourself in a reactive gel to reduce the attack's success tier by 1 and cause acid harm to the attacker equal to your proficiency bonus.
7. Osmotic Overdrive: You gain 50% resistance to acid and fire damage. If you already have either, gain immunity instead.

8. Chain Reaction: Whenever you cause harm with your Volatile Throw, you can expend one additional use of it to have it chain to another location within 10' of the original, causing half the amount of harm.
9. Perfected Formula: You ignore resistance to acid and fire damage, and the damage dice of your Volatile Throw increase to d20s.

10. Apotheosis of Alchemy: Whenever your Volatile Throw bombs explode, their areas remain as a persistent zone of lingering vapours for the remainder of combat. The zone causes 2d6 acid harm to creatures and counts as difficult terrain for creatures other than you.

theme: manifesting a sword from your spirit
tiers: 1. Spectral Sword: As an action, you can call into your main hand a ghostly sword formed from your spirit, so long as you aren't wielding anything else there. The Spectral Sword is a martial melee weapon of the sword category that you have proficiency in. It deals 1d8 + STR/DEX psychic damage and has the Deadly, Responsive, and Scaling (+1) traits.
2. Phantom Weapon: Your Spectral Sword's base damage ignores resistance and immunity.
3. Ghostly Spin: You gain +1 weapon AB while wielding your Spectral Sword.
4. Focused Spirit: You add your proficiency bonus to the damage of your Spectral Sword.

5. Twin Phantoms: If your offhand is free when you conjure your Spectral Sword, you also summon a second Spectral Sword in your offhand. It increases the damage die size of your main hand Spectral Sword to 1d12 and increases its Scaling trait to +3.
6. Ethereal Cleave: Whenever you hit a creature with your Spectral Sword, you may cause psychic harm equal to half the damage dealt to another creature adjacent to the target.
7. Unfading Edge: Your Ghostly Spin now grants +4 weapon AB and +3 weapon damage while wielding your Spectral Sword.
8. Ward of the Blade: You gain 50% physical resistance while wielding your Spectral Sword.
9. Soulforged Mastery: Whenever you deal psychic damage with your Spectral Sword, you heal HP equal to half the psychic damage dealt.

10. Manifest Heartcleaver: Once per long rest, as a free action while holding two Spectral Swords, you can transform them into the Heartcleaver for the next hour. The Heartcleaver is a martial melee weapon of the sword category that you have proficiency in. It deals 3d6 psychic damage + 1d8 radiant damage + STR/DEX and has the Deadly, Responsive, Two-Handed, and Scaling (+11) traits. It counts as a Spectral Sword for the purposes of this glyph path's other features.
1. Earthen Resilience: Whenever you would be debilitated, restrained, or staggered by a fortitude attack, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
2. Glimmer of Stone: Your melee attacks ignore resistance and immunity.
3. Elemental Stoneskin: You gain 50% resistance to poison damage and whenever you would be poisoned, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
4. Petrifying Aura: You radiate a 5' aura of petrifying energy. Foes within the aura have -5' Speed.
5. Granite Carapace: Your skin and bones harden, granting you +1 armour. Additionally, you gain +5 physical resistance.
6. Stone's Refuge: You gain 50% resistance to physical damage.
7. Natural Stone Form: Once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 HP, you may instead drop to 1 HP and become incapacitated and immune to damage and harm for 1 round.
8. Aura of Stonelike Might: Your Petrifying Aura's range increases to 10', and foes within it have -1 AB and -1 to ability checks.
9. Flesh to Stone: Once per long rest, you can cast Investiture of Stone.
10. Avatar of Petrified Majesty: You gain +60' of truesight, and all of your damage and harm is always non-lethal as you temporarily petrify your targets instead of killing them.

theme: becoming a vessel for an eldritch being
tiers: 1. Void Touched: You gain +30' of darkvision.
2. Unsettling Whispers: You can cast the Message cantrip at will.
3. Shrouded Form: You have advantage on Stealth checks while in dim light or darkness.
4. Eldritch Fortitude: Whenever you would become charmed or frightened, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
5. Void Ward: Once per short rest, upon failing a save, you may roll a d6 and add its result to the save.
6. Tendrils of the Void: Your damaging attacks deal additional necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
7. Cosmic Resilience: You gain 50% resistance to psychic damage. Additionally, while in dim light or darkness, you gain 50% resistance to all damage.
8. Aura of the Unknown: Creatures within 10' of you have disadvantage on Perception checks to detect your presence. If you're in dim light or darkness, this aura extends to 20'.
9. Eyes of Oblivion: You gain an additional +30' of darkvision, and +10' of truesight.

10. Herald of the Void: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you can shapeshift into the tendrilled form of the creature within you for the remainder of combat. In this form, you gain fly speed equal to your Speed, 50% resistance to all damage except force, and you radiate a 5' persistent zone that causes 3d6 necrotic harm to foes.

theme: accessing power from your past lives
tiers: 1. Faint Memory: Gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.
2. Reincarnation's Boon: Once per long rest, upon being reduced to 0 HP, you may cast Skill Empowerment on yourself, boosting your Faint Memory skill.
3. Lingering Echo: Once per short rest, you may reroll a failed ability check or save. You must use the new roll.
4. Residual Expertise: Gain an expertise die in your Faint Memory skill.
5. Past Whispers: You learn one cantrip from the Wizard spell list that you can cast at will, governing it with any ability.
6. Ancestral Recall: Once per short rest, you can add a d8 to any ability check, attack roll, or save. You do this after the roll is made, but before the outcome is determined.
7. Echoing Endurance: Once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 HP, you may instead remain at 1 HP.

8. Soulbound Talent: Whenever you cast your Past Whispers cantrip, treat it as if your level were 5 higher. If it deals damage, you also add your proficiency bonus to its damage. Addiionally, if you wish, you may immediately change your Past Whispers cantrip.
9. Past Life Resurgence: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you can call upon an echo of a former self until the remainder of combat. During this time, you gain +1 to all defences.

10. Eternal Echoes: All features from this glyph path that recharge on a short or long rest now also recharge at the start of each round in combat. Additionally, whenever you use Past Life Resurgence, you may choose an ally within 30' of you to also benefit from its effects.
1. Twin's Harmony: While dual-wielding weapons of the axe, knife, polearm, or sword (Bladed) categories, you gain +1 weapon AB.
2. Balanced Blade: All one-handed Bladed weapons gain the Offhand (no effect) trait for you. Their other traits have no effect.
3. Swift Edge: Your weapon critical successs while dual-wielding Bladed weapons deal additional damage equal to your main hand weapon's base damage.
4. Crosscut: Your weapon major successs while dual-wielding Bladed weapons deal 1d6 additional base damage.
5. Precision Riposte: While dual-wielding Bladed weapons, you gain +1 weapon critical success range.
6. Vortex Blade: Whenever you score a weapon major success while dual-wielding Bladed weapons, foes adjacent to you suffer 2d6 slashing harm.
7. Resolute Strikes: Whenever you score a weapon major success while dual-wielding Bladed weapons, gain an amount of temporary HP equal to your level.
8. Blade Tempest: Whenever you take the Attack action while dual-wielding Bladed weapons, you may attack two different creatures within your reach, with each attack being reduced by 1 success tier.
9. Defensive Flourish: While dual-wielding Bladed weapons, gain 50% resistance to slashing damage.
10. Ever-Dancing Blades: While dual-wielding Bladed weapons, your weapon attacks deal 2d6 additional force damage, as a spectral echo of your Offhand weapon strikes.
1. Hardened Exoskeleton: While unarmoured, you gain +1 armour.

2. Moisture Holding: You no longer need to drink water, are immune to dehydration, and are immune to diseases and toxins delivered through water. This reduces the gold cost of each journey day of travel by 1, to a minimum of 0.
3. Earthbound Awareness: You gain 5' of tremorsense while on the ground.
4. Acidic Spit: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can spit acid at a creature within 15', causing 1d4 acid harm.
5. Armoured Plating: Your Hardened Exoskeleton's armour bonus increases to +2.
6. Regenerative Carapace: Whenever you finish a short rest, you regain HP equal to your level.
7. Burrow Mastery: You gain burrow speed equal to your Speed. Your burrow speed suffers no resistance from non-magical, unworked earth.
8. Enhanced Tremorsense: Your Earthbound Awareness' tremorsense increases to 30'. Additionally, you can see through up to 1 foot of stone or earth.

9. Impenetrable Casing: At the start of each of your turns while on the ground, you may curl up into an armoured ball until you uncurl as a free action. While curled, you gain immunity to physical damage and your speeds are reduced to 0.

10. Exoskeletal Metamorphosis: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you may shapeshift into a Colossal Isopod for the remainder of combat. In this form, your size increases by 1, your armour increases by 2, you gain 30' of tremorsense, and fortitude attacks have disadvantage against you. However, you cannot cast spells in this form and your weapons are replaced with a Bite attack that deals 2d10 + STR piercing damage and has the Scaling (+7) trait.
1. Prismalight: You can cast the Light cantrip at will. When you do so, its light rotates through the colours of the rainbow.
2. Radiant Echo: Once per long rest, after making a damaging attack, you can add 1d4 radiant damage to it.
3. Chromatic Glow: You gain 50% resistance to radiant damage. If you already have 50% resistance, gain immunity instead.

4. Prismatic Ray: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can fire a beam of rainbow light at a creature within 60' of you. It causes 1d4 radiant harm, and the target must makes a save. On a fail, it is blinded for 1 round.

5. Spectrum Push: Whenever you deal radiant damage or cause radiant harm to a creature, you may push the target 5' away from you. You can do this a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.
6. Radiant Retribution: Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker suffers an amount of radiant harm equal to your proficiency bonus.
7. Prism Shield: You gain 50% resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, and necrotic damage.
8. Gleaming Ward: Once per short rest, when targeted by an attack, you can reduce its success tier by 1.
9. Daylight's Favour: You can cast the Daylight spell at will. When you do so, its light rotates through the colours of the rainbow.
10. Spectrum Sovereign: Whenever you would roll dice for radiant damage or harm, instead treat all dice as having rolled their maximum value.

theme: fighting with nothing but your own body
tiers: 1. Unarmed Proficiency: You gain proficiency with brawling weapons and you gain +1 weapon AB while wielding them. Additionally, their base damage die size is increased by 1 and they gain the Scaling (+1) trait.
2. Reinforced Strike: You deal +1 unarmed damage.
3. Shattering Blow: Once per short rest, after hitting with an unarmed attack, you can add 1d4 thunder damage to the attack's damage.
4. Iron Parry: Once per short rest, when you are targeted by a melee attack, you can reduce its success tier by 1.
5. Pressure Point: Once per short rest, after hitting with an unarmed attack, you can give the target disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.
6. Resonant Kick: Once per long rest, as a free action, you can cause 1d4 thunder harm to all adjacent creatures.
7. Phase Step: Once per short rest, when you hit with an unarmed attack, you may immediately teleport up to 10' to an unoccupied space.

8. Fist of the Unbroken Storm: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you may channel the storm's fury into your unarmed attacks for the remainder of combat. During this time, you gain +1 unarmed critical success range and your unarmed attacks ignore physical resistance. Additionally, your unarmed attacks deal 2d6 additional thunder damage.
9. Unbreakable Body: While wielding a brawling weapon, you gain +1 armour and 50% resistance to bludgeoning damage.

10. Mastery of the Unbound: Your unarmed attacks ignore physical resistance and immunity and deal 2d8 additional force damage. Additionally, you have +2 unarmed critical success range and whenever you score a critical success with an unarmed attack, all foes within 10' of you lose HP equal to half the attack's damage as a shockwave erupts from you.
1. Druidcraft Bloom: You can cast the Druidcraft cantrip at will. Whenever you use it to manipulate plants, its range is doubled.
2. Rootstride: You ignore difficult terrain caused by plants.
3. Thorn Whip Mastery: You can cast the Thorn Whip cantrip at will. Its pull distance increases to 20 feet.
4. Entangling Roots: Once per long rest, you can cast the Entangle spell.

5. Root Ward: Once per long rest, when you or an ally within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can cause roots to surge from the ground between attacker and target, reducing the attack's damage by 1d12.
6. Deepening Roots: Your Root Ward can now be used twice per long rest. Additionally, whenever you cast Entangle with your Entangling Roots, its fortitude attack has advantage.
7. Ironbark Skin: Allies within 60 feet of you gain the effects of the Barkskin spell.
8. Master of Roots: Once per long rest, you can cast either Plant Growth or Awaken. When you cast Awaken this way, the awakened plant's maximum HP is increased by 24.
9. Overgrown Bastion: Once per long rest, you can cast the Wall of Thorns spell.

10. Earthbound Avatar: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you can merge with the earth for the remainder of combat. While doing this, you gain 60' of tremorsense and +3 armour. You also gain the ability to slam adjacent creatures as a free action, causing 1d4 bludgeoning harm. Finally, once per round when a creature ends its turn within 15' of you, you can teleport to an unoccupied space on solid ground within 30' of that creature.

1. Echoed Presence: Once per short rest, as a free action, you project a faint overlay of your avatar over your body that lasts until you fall unconscious or make an attack. You determine what it looks like, but it must match your creature type and size. While the overlay is active, you have +1 armour and gain advantage on one skill check you make.
2. Buffer Circuit: Whenever you would take damage, you can reduce that damage by 6. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus between long rests.

3. Networked Reflexes: You gain +10' of Speed, and can take the Dash, Disengage, and Hide actions as bonus actions. Whenever you use these actions as bonus actions, you also grant incoming reflex attacks disadvantage for 1 round.

4. Augmented Interface: You learn a 1st-level wizard or warlock spell that has a casting time of 1 action, which you can cast once per long rest, governed by any ability. Whenever you cast it, any damage it deals is increased by 1d6 force damage, and any healing it grants is increased by the same amount.

5. Phased Form: Once per long rest, as a free action, you can become partially incorporeal for 1 round, granting you advantage on all saves and Dexterity-based checks, and immunity to physical damage.

6. Distributed Cognition: You gain 120' of telepathy that only works with willing creatures and can see through one willing creature's senses within that range for up to 1 hour total per long rest. While sharing senses, you have advantage on Investigation and Perception checks.

7. Static Resonance: Whenever you finish a long rest, you can gain either +1 AB or +1 to saves, both of which last until you finish a long rest. Additionally, you permanently gain 30' of darkvision. Finally, once per short rest, you can add your proficiency bonus to a save you make.

8. Hardened Shell: You gain 50% resistance to physical, fire, cold, lightning, acid, and poison damage. Additionally, once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 HP, you may instead remain at 1 HP and your avatar emits a burst that knocks all adjacent creatures of your choice prone.

9. Avatar Ascension: When you gain this feature, choose one damage type to gain immunity to permanently. Additionally, while bloodied, you gain +10 passive regeneration. Finally, once per long rest as a free action, you may manifest an avatar projection within 60' of you, a large creature that can take actions you command, but cannot make attacks or be targeted in combat.

10. Avatar Transcendence: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you may shapeshift into your avatar for the remainder of combat. While in this form, you treat your creature type as a construct and nothing else, gain a flying speed equal to your Speed and a climb speed equal to half, deal 3d8 additional force damage with your damaging attacks, and can use a free action to cast the Mirror Image spell (2 duplicates only) on yourself. If you drop to 0 HP while in this form, the effect immediately ends and you are debilitated for the remainder of combat.
1. Lingering Chill: Whenever you hit a creature with a melee attack, it suffers 1d4 cold harm at the start of its next turn, and has disadvantage on the first save it makes in the next round.
2. Quieting Touch: Once per short rest, when you hit with an attack, you can grant the target disadvantage on its first save prompted by you in the next round.
3. Haze of Fatigue: Whenever you bloody a creature, it makes a save, gaining a level of fatigue on a fail.
4. Blinding Echo: Once per long rest, when you inflict a condition on a creature, you can also impose disadvantage on the target's first attack roll in the next round.

5. Crippling Sigil: Whenever you score a major success against a creature, you can brand it for 1 minute, or until you brand another creature. While branded, a creature has -10' Speed and -1 to all saves. You can do this a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.
6. Mind-Needle: Once per short rest, when you score a major success against a creature, you may immediately break its concentration and grant it disadvantage on opportunity attacks for 1 round.

7. Sapping Field: Once per short rest, when a creature ends its turn within 10' of you, you can force it to make a save. On a fail, you choose to either blind or stagger it for 1 round, or grant it a level of fatigue.

8. Warding of Weakness: Whenever you affect a creature with your Lingering Chill or Crippling Sigil, you may choose another creature within 15' of it to suffer 1 cold harm at the start of its next turn, or -5' Speed for the brand's duration, respectively.

9. Mastery of Maladies: Once per long rest, when you apply one of the following effects, you can escalate it, granting the improved effect in brackets and increasing the effect's duration to 1 minute or until the target passes a passive save: Haze of Fatigue's fatigue (2 levels of fatigue); Blinding Echo's disadvantage (blind); Crippling Sigil's Speed reduction (sluggish).

10. Curse of the Deep Bind: Once per long rest, as a free action, you can unleash a powerful binding curse on a creature within 60' of you. The target must make a save, becoming your choice of blinded, dazed, or staggered for 1 minute. The target may make passive saves to end this effect early, but if they fail 2 in a row, they stop making passive saves and are also debilitated for the remaining duration. If a creature succeeds on its initial save against this effect, it becomes Sluggish and has disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 minute instead.
1. Luminous Lantern: You emit 10' of bright light and 10' of dim light while conscious. You can extinguish or reignite this light as a free action.

2. Radiant Senses: While your Luminous Lantern is active, you have advantage on sight-based Perception checks and can see through magical darkness created by spells of 2nd-level or lower. Additionally, if you have any amount of darkvision, its range is increased by 30'.

3. Beacon's Warmth: Whenever you or an ally starts their turn within your Luminous Lantern's bright light, that creature regains HP equal to your level. A creature can only benefit from this once per short rest. Additionally, your hit dice heal +2 HP while your Luminous Lantern is active during short rests.

4. Revealing Glimmer: You and allies within your Luminous Lantern's bright light can sense invisible creatures and objects, and whenever any of you would be blinded, charmed, or frightened by a creature with Dexterity as its highest ability, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.

5. Blinding Edge: Whenever you deal radiant damage, you may deal 2d8 additional radiant damage. Additionally, if that attack scored a major success against a creature that is within you Luminous Lantern's bright light, it is blinded for 1 round. You can use this feature a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.

6. Beacon Ward: While within your Luminous Lantern's bright light, you and allies gain 50% resistance to necrotic damage and have a +1 bonus to all defences. Additionally, once per long rest, when a creature within that light would be reduced to 0 HP, you may choose to keep them at 1 HP instead.

7. Radiant Stride: While in bright light, you gain flying speed equal to half your Speed for up to 1 minute total per short rest. While flying this way, you do not provoke opportunity attacks from creatures with Dexterity as their highest ability.

8. Beaconburst: Once per long rest, as a free action, you detonate a controlled burst of brilliant light. All foes within 30' suffer 1d8 radiant harm, and then make a save. On a fail, they are blinded for the remainder of combat. Undead and creatures within your Luminous Lantern's bright light have disadvantage on this save.

9. Halo of Purity: Your Luminous Lantern's bright light radius increases to 60', and you and allies within this light have +1 to death saves. Additionally, the damage dice of your Beaconburst increase to d10s, and creatures that fail the save are banished to a plane of shadow-twisted void until they pass a passive save. When they return, they immediately take a turn. Finally, allies who start their turns within your Luminous Lantern's bright light remove either the debilitated, poisoned, charmed, blinded, or staggered condition from themselves, but a creature can only do so once per long rest.

10. Avatar of Luminous Sovereignty: While in bright light, you have immunity to radiant damage and being blinded. Additionally, the damage dice of your Beaconburst increase to d12s, and while its targets are banished, they suffer 4d8 ongoing radiant harm. Finally, once per long rest when you roll for initiative, you may shapeshift into a being of light for the remainder of combat. In this form, you shed bright light in a 120' radius and dim for an additional 120', gain +3 armour, gain advantage on all saves, gain fly speed equal to your Speed, and your melee attacks deal additional radiant damage equal to your proficiency bonus. When this shapeshift ends, you gain a level of fatigue.

1. Thought Reach: As a free action, you can pick up or move up to 10' one unattended object that weights no more than 1kg and is within 10' of you. You can do this a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.

2. Mental Nudge: Whenever you use Thought Reach, you may instead target a Small or Medium creature. When you do so, the target makes a save. On a fail, you push it 5' in a direction of your choice, and it has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

3. Kinetic Fingers: The object weight limit for your Thought Reach increases to 5kg, and its range/movement distance increases to 30'. Additionally, you can now use it to open unlocked doors and containers.

4. Telekinetic Tap: Whenever you use Thought Reach to move an object, you can now use it to strike a creature within its range. The creature suffers 1d4 harm of a physical type based on the object (or 2d4, if the object weighs 2+kg). If you use Thought Reach to directly push a creature, it suffers the bludgeoning harm as if being struck by a light object.

5. Featherstep Levitation: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can begin levitating 10' off the ground for a number of rounds equal to your proficiency bonus. Whenever you would be restrained or grappled while levitating in this way, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success. You can move horizontally at half your Speed while levitating.

6. Remote Motion: Your Thought Reach's range/movement distance increases to 60', and you may control up to two objects at once with it so long as their combined weight does not exceed the weight limit. The harm caused by Telekinetic Tap also increases by one die size.

7. Path of the Mind's Stride: Your Featherstep Levitation's duration increases to 1 minute. Additionally, while it is active, you may move across vertical surfaces as if they were the ground, move through spaces as small as 1 inch wide without squeezing, and shift whenever you move. Additionally, you can modify your base hovering height between 10' and 40' as part of your movement.

8. Telekinetic Grasp: As a free action, you can attempt to restrain a Large or smaller creature within 60' of you. The target makes a save, becoming restrained until it passes a passive save on a fail. This feature requires your concentration.

9. Mindstep: Once per long rest, as a free action, you and a willing creature of your size or smaller that you are touching both teleport 120'. After doing so, your Telekinetic Tap's causes 1d4 additional psychic harm, and creatures restrained by your Telekinetic Grasp suffer ongoing psychic harm equal to your proficiency bonus. If you use this feature while your Featherstep Levitation is active, your Levitation immediately ends.

10. Mindway Mastery: The ranges/movement distances for all of this glyph path's features increase to 300'. Your Thought Reach can now maintain control of up to 3 objects at once, with a total weight limit of 100kg, and your Telekinetic Grasp can now restrain Huge or smaller creatures. Your Telekinetic Grasp no longer requires your concentration, but you can still only restrain one creature at a time. Your Mindstep can now be used once per short rest, you can bring up to 6 willing creatures with you, and you may choose to teleport any of them up to 60' away from your destination instead of the destination itself. Finally, your Telekinetic Tap now causes 1d6 additional force harm.
1. Draconic Tinge: When you gain this feature, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. This is your Aura Type. You gain 50% resistance to your Aura Type.
2. Scent of Wyrm: You have advantage on history checks to recall lore about dragons, gain +1 intimidation vs dragons, and gain +1 to survival checks to track dragons.
3. Elemental Skin: Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker suffers 1d4 harm of your Aura Type.

4. Aura Whisper: As a free action, you can emit a faint draconic rumble that grants allies within 10' 8 temporary HP. The first melee attack these allies make while they have this temporary HP deals 1d4 additional damage of your Aura Type. You can use this feature a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.
5. Breathling: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can exhale a 30' line of your Aura Type. Creatures in the area suffer 1d4 harm.
6. Wyrmward: Whenever you use Breathling, adjacent allies gain +1 resistance to your Aura Type for 1 round.

7. Dragon's Reach: Whenever you or an ally within 15' of you would become frightened, that creature makes a save, ignoring the condition on a success. Additionally, once per long rest when you score a major success with a melee attack, you can push the target 10' away and knock it prone as draconic force lashes out.

8. Scaled Bulwark: At the start of each of your turns, you and allies within 10' of you gain 2 temporary HP. Additionally, once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 HP, you can drop to 1 HP instead and emit a protective shell that grants you and allies within 10' of you 50% resistance to all damage from a single creature of your choice until the start of your next turn.

9. Ancient Resonance: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you can weave your aura into your attacks for the remainder of combat, granting you the following benefits. Your damaging attacks deal 1d8 additional Aura Type damage. You also project a 5' persistent zone that causes 1d8 harm of your Aura Type to foes. And finally, your Elemental Skin causes 2 additional dice of harm.

10. Wyrmform Sovereign: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you can shapeshift into a partial wyrmform for the remainder of combat. While in this form, you project a 15' persistent zone that causes 2d8 harm of your Aura Type to foes, gain +2 armour, are immune to being frightened, gain fly speed equal to your Speed, and can use your Breathling twice this combat, causing 3 additional dice of harm and increasing all the dice to d6s.

1. Apex Sense: You always know which foe in combat has the highest current HP, which is referred to as the Apex. Additionally, you always know the direction to the creature with the highest current HP within 1km.
2. Hunter's Thread: You gain an expertise die in survival checks to locate or track creatures with a higher CR than your level.
3. True Sightline: You ignore disadvantage caused by long range and cover when attacking the Apex.

4. Unrelenting Path: If the Apex is 30+' away from you at the start of your turn, you ignore difficult terrain that turn, and if you end your movement that turn adjacent to the Apex, you gain advantage on attacks you make against it that turn.

5. Predator's Gaze: You cannot be surprised. Additionally, your initiative rolls are always at least 1 more than the Apex's and you cannot be frightened by it. Finally, once per long rest, when you score a major success against the Apex, it becomes sluggish and has disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 round.
6. Focused Strike: Whenever you attack the Apex, you have +1 AB and deal +1 damage.

7. Threaded Mark: Whenever you hit the Apex, you can mark it for the remainder of combat, or until you mark another creature. You deal 1d6 additional base damage to the marked creature, and allies in your line of sight have advantage on attack rolls against it.
8. Apex Anchor: Creatures affected by your Threaded Mark cannot willingly move beyond 30' from you (except towards you), unless they teleport.
9. Piercing Focus: Your bonus from Focused Strike increases to +2 AB and its additional damage is doubled.

10. Apex Strike: As a free action, project a single, unstoppable bolt of planar energy at the Apex. You do not need line of sight to the target to use this feature. The target suffers 5d4 force harm and makes a save. On a fail, it gains an upgraded Threaded Mark that adds 5 additional dice of base damage. Regardless, the target loses any invisibility it may have had. After you use this feature, all features in this glyph path except for Apex Sense are disabled until you finish a long rest.
1. Liminal Step: You ignore difficult terrain and cannot be grappled by nonmagical means.

2. Pocket Fold: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can create a tiny folded space around one object you are carrying (no larger than 5' on a side). The object becomes weightless and is inaccessible until you dismiss the fold or take it out as a bonus action. The object is still visible, but material things pass through it as if it were light.

3. Blinkway: Once per short rest, you may replace the first 15' of your movement on a turn with 15' of teleportation. When you teleport in this way, you leave behind a faint shimmer that lingers until the end of your next turn. Creatures that end their turn in that shimmer are immune to damage but have disadvantage on opportunity attacks.
4. Ethereal Tether: You have 50% resistance to force damage and can move through creatures and nonmagical objects as if they were difficult terrain, but must end your movement in an unoccupied space.

5. Swaptrace: Once per long rest, when you or a creature you can see within 30' would be hit by an attack, you can instantly swap that creature's position with an unoccupied space within 30' of you. The attack still hits if the target is still within its reach, range, or area.

6. Planar Siphon: You can now use Swaptrace twice between long rests, and your Blinkway replaces 30' of movement. Additionally, whenever you use Swaptrace, you may choose to siphon a tiny sliver of planar energy into the repositioned creature's space. The target gains one of the following effects of your choice for 1 round: disadvantage on incoming reflex attacks, advantage on Strength checks, or 50% resistance to fire.

7. Folding Corridor: Once per long rest, as a free action, you can create a short planar fold: a 5'-wide, straight corridor up to 60' long that lasts 1 minute. The corridor occupies a line of contiguous spaces and is visible as a seam of shimmering light. Creatures may move through the corridor normally, ignoring any material obstacles in the corridor's spaces. Creatures within the corridor have disadvantage on Perception checks to perceive outside of the corridor.
8. Seammastery: Your Folding Corridor can now be up to 120' long and lasts 1 hour. Additionally, the planar energy effects from your Planar Siphon now last 1 hour.

9. Planar Stain: Whenever you create a Folding Corridor, the end of the corridor furthest from you leaves a 20'-radius stain centred on it for the same duration as the corridor. Choose one of the following planar effects for the stain to have: the area is dim light and creatures have advantage on stealth checks to hide in it; nonmagical flammable items in the area do not ignite; spells in the area have no vocalised component. The stain is also a persistent zone that forces foes to make a save, being pushed 10' into the corridor on a fail.

10. Weaveworld's Threshold: Once per long rest, as a free action, you create a transient planar doorway that lasts for 1 minute (requires concentration) and links your current location to a point in within 1km on the same plane as you, or on a similar point on the Ethereal plane. The doorway is a 10'-diameter portal that remains anchored to the ground. Creatures may pass through freely. When a creature entes the doorway you may optionally cause one of the following planar effects once per creature that passes: swap its position with a willing creature within 60' of you; teleport it to an unoccupied space within 120' of you; banish it to a pocket dimension until the start of your next turn.
1. Balanced Edge (strong): You gain +1 weapon AB while wielding a knife weapon. Additionally, this bonus is doubled while you are attacking alongside a basic maneuver.
2. Quick Flick: The base damage die of your knife weapons is doubled.
3. Keen Footwork (strong): Whenever you move at least 10' on your turn immediately before making a knife attack, that attack roll gains an expertise die.

4. Minor Bleeding Strike: Whenever you hit with a knife attack, you can cause 1d4 ongoing slashing harm to the target until it passes a passive save (does not stack). You can use this feature a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.
5. Ghostblade Step: Whenever you take the Disengage action, you leave behind an echo of movement after moving away. Until the end of your next turn, opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage.

6. Precise Rend: Your critical damage bonus with knives is increased by your level. Additionally, whenever you score a critical success with a knife weapon against a creature suffering from your Minor Bleeding Strike, the ongoing harm increases by an additional die.

7. Dancing Parry (strong): Whenever you are targeted by a melee attack while wielding a knife weapon, you can reduce the attack's success tier by 1. If the attack still hits, the attacker suffers slashing harm equal to your knife's base damage die.

8. Slice of Silence: Once per short rest, when you hit with a knife attack while hidden, you do not reveal yourself, and if it scored a major success, the target also has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.
9. Whirling Torrent: Your Quick Flick now triples the base damage die of your knife weapons.

10. Bladesong Crescendo: Once per long rest, as a free action, you enter a bladesong stance for the remainder of combat. During this time, you grant incoming reflex attacks disadvantage, gain 50% resistance to slashing damage, increase your Speed by 20', and whenever you score a major success with a knife attack, you can forgo any damage to knock the target prone and push it 10' away. If the attack was a critical success, the target is restrained until it breaks free as an action instead of prone. You can end the restrain early as a free action to cause necrotic harm equal to your main hand weapon's base damage die plus 4d6.
1. Grain Grip: Whenever you would be knocked prone while in contact with sand or soil, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success. Additionally, you ignore sand-based difficult terrain.

2. Sand Whisper: Twice per long rest, you can spend 5 minutes concentrating on sand within 30' of you to cause it to form a single line of shifting runes or a small pattern that conveys a simple message (up to 25 words) legible to creatures of your choice for 1 minute.

3. Sand Skin: While in contact with sand, you have +1 armour vs ranged weapon attacks. Additionally, if you spend 1 minute embedded in loose sand, you gain advantage on your next stealth check made in the next hour.
4. Sifting Step: While standing on sand, you have +5' Speed, and may take the Dash action as a bonus action once per short rest while standing on sand or soil.

5. Dust Cloak: Once per short rest, when you are attacked, you can surround yourself with a swirling veil of sand for 1 round, granting the triggering attack disadvantage and giving all melee attacks against you -1 AB. While this is active, you count as being in contact with sand.

6. Glassvein Strike: Once per short rest when you make an attack while standing on sand or within 10' of sand, you can cause the stand to strike with you, adding 1d8 force damage to the attack. On a major success, the target is also restrained by sand until the end of your next turn. On a hit, the target is sluggish for the same duration.

7. Sandward Bastion: Once per long rest, as a free action, you create a 15'-radius dome of compacted sand centred on you that last for 1 minute. The dome counts as half cover and reduces the success tier of ranged attacks passing through it by 1. When you create the dome, you can include two 10' exists you designate.

8. Quicksand Field: Once per long rest, as a free action, you transform a 30' square area of ground within 60' of you into quicksand for 1 minute. The quicksand is a persistent zone that forces creatures to make a save or become grappled and restrained. A creature can escape by using its action and making a brawn check against your standard DC. Creatures within the area are heavily obscured from creatures more than 60' away from them.

9. Sandstorm Siege: Once per long rest, as a free action, you create a swirling sandstorm in a 60' radius centred on a point within 120' of you. The area is heavily obscured, creatures are blinded inside, and all fly speeds are reduced to 0 within it. It is also a persistent zone that causes 4d6 slashing harm.

10. Hourglass Sovereignty: You gain 60' of truesight while standing on sand or soil, your Sandstorm Siege now causes 6d10 slashing harm, your Dust Cloak now lasts 2 rounds, and once per long rest you may spend 10 minutes doing nothing to permanently turn up to an 100' square of nonmagical terrain into sand.

1. Whisperseed: You can speak one short sentence (up to 25 words) privately to one creature within 30' of you. The target hears the words in their mind and understands them in their primary language if they know any language; otherwise they perceive an intelligible image. The message is private and cannot be overheard by creatures more than 5' away from either participant.
2. Echo Anchor: Your Whisperseed range increases to 60'.
3. Veil of Dialects: If the target of your Whisperseed doesn't know any language, it receives a clear mental summary of your sentence.
4. Secret Knot: Your Whisperseed no longer requires line of sight to the target and creatures within 5' of the participants can no longer overhear the sentence.

5. Chosen Bond: During a short or long rest, you can touch a creature to form a bond with them. While bonded, you may use Whisperseed once per long rest at a range of up to 1km. The bond lasts until you form a new one.
6. Silent Relay: Your Chosen Bond's range increases to 6km, and it can function across overlapping planes.

7. Veiled Channel: As a free action, you can open a private communication channel to your Chosen Bond creature that lasts for up to 10 minutes or until you end it. While open, you and the bonded creature can converse freely using your Chosen Bond. The channel blocks all divination spells and similar effects from revealing the conversation. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus between long rests.

8. Remote Tongue: Your Veiled Channel can now be used without expending one of its uses if both you and the bonded creature are not adjacent to any creatures within your party and are separated by at least 300'.

9. Soulcloak: Any conversation through your Chosen Bond is masked from detection as per your Veiled Channel, and neither participant can be compelled to reveal the content of its communication unwillingly while the bond exists.

10. Echo of One: 24 hours after your Chosen Bond ends with a creature, that creature cannot recall any information about what was conversed about through your bond. The only thing they remember is whether or not what they stated in those communications was sincere or not.

1. Scented Weapon: Your main hand weapon is imbued with a faint, pleasant scent. You have advantage on perception checks based on smell and gain a +1 bonus to persuasion and nature checks made to calm beasts and non-hostile humanoids that can smell you. This affects the Befriend Animal journey activity.

2. Lingering Trace: Your Scented Weapon's scent now lingers on creatures hit by it for 1 minute. While the scent is present, those creatures have disadvantage on perception checks to locate creatures by scent, and you gain advantage on survival checks to track those creatures by scent.

3. Aromatic Flourish: Once per short rest when you score a major success with your Scented Weapon, you can add aromatic flourish to give the target disdavantage on its next attack roll and ability check before the end of your next turn.
4. Intensified Flourish: Your Aromatic Flourish can now be used on a standard hit.

5. Perfume Burst: Once per long rest, as a free action, you can release a powerful scent from your weapon in a 30' cone. Each creature inside that can breathe and smell must make a save, becoming dazed until it passes a passive save on a fail. A creature that passes this save becomes immune to this feature for 24 hours.
6. Refined Burst: You can now use Perfume Burst twice between long rests, and creatures that fail its save are also sluggish and have -2 reflex until the effect ends.

7. Scent of Dominion: Whenever you hit a creature with your Scented Weapon, you can mark it with your scent until you dismiss the mark or 24 hours have passed. Will attacks against the marked creature have advantage while it is within 60' of you. You can have a number of creatures marked at once equal to your proficiency bonus.

8. Bouquet of Warding: You and up to 1 willing creature adjacent to you gain a +1 bonus to armour, and whenever they would be frightened or charmed, they make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
9. Potent Bouquet: Your Bouquet of Warding's range increases to 10', and affected creatures become immune to being frightened and charmed.
10. Sovereign Aroma: Your Scent of Dominion remains active while you are within 120' of the target, and the number of creatures you can have marked increases to double your proficiency bonus.
1. Steady Hands: You gain a +1 bonus to AB and damage with blowguns.
2. Poison Salve: Whenever you hit a creature with a blowgun attack, the target suffers 1 ongoing poison harm, stacking until it passes a passive save.
3. Mild Agonist: Whenever you score a major success with a blowgun attack, the target suffers 1d4 psychic harm and the next attack against it before the end of your next turn has advantage.

4. Targeted Pharmacokinetics: Once per long rest, when you would apply Mild Agonist, you may change the attack advantage effect into one of the following: target is sluggish for 1 round; target suffers 1d6 additional necrotic harm; target has disadvantage on perception checks until it passes a passive save.
5. Rapid Diffuser: Whenever you apply a negative effect with a blowgun attack from this path, all foes adjacent to the target also gain the effect.
6. Countermeasure Binder: The first time a creature fails its passive save for Poison Salve, it gains disadvantage to that same passive save until it takes a long rest.
7. Synergist Protocol: While a creature is affected by Countermeasure Binder, it also has -1 to those saves.

8. Overdose Catalyst: Once per long rest, when you hit with two blowgun attacks in a row in a single combat, you can increase the second attack's success tier by 1, and if that would make the attack a critical success, the target suffers 6d6 poison harm and is dazed for 1 round. Otherwise they suffer 4d6 with no other effect. When you use this feature, Mild Agonist's harm is increased to 2d6 for the second attack.
9. Potent Carrier: Your Mild Agonist's psychic harm increases to 1d6, and it triggers on standard hits as well.

10. Apotheotic Transfusion: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you may inject a perfected compound into yourself. For the remainder of combat, you gain immunity to poison damage and have advantage on blowgun attacks. After the combat, you gain a level of fatigue.
1. Sensitive Ears: You gain advantage on perception checks related to hearing.
2. Humanlike Expression: You gain an expertise die in persuasion.
3. Scent Trail: You have advantage on survival checks to track creatures that have a scent, and you can always pinpoint the direction of a creature within 30' that you can smell.

4. Facecall: Once per short or long rest, when you roll for initiative, you may shapeshift into a jinmenken for the remainder of combat. In this form, you emit a 10' persistent zone that forces foes to make a save, becoming charmed by you until the form ends on a fail. A creature that passes the save is immune to this effect until it takes a long rest.
5. Deepened Expression: While interacting with no more than 5 creatures at once, you have advantage on deception and persuasion checks against creatures that can see your face.
6. Canine Instincts: Will attacks that you can sense have disadvantage against you. Additionally, you gain an expertise die on initiative rolls.

7. Feral Resilience: You gain 50% resistance to psychic damage and whenever you would become charmed, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success. Additionally, once per long rest when you would be reduced to 0 HP, drop to 1 HP instead until the end of your next turn when you drop to 0 if you haven't already.
8. Hardened Face: The save from your Facecall persistent area is now made with disadvantage, and creatures charmed by it are also rattled.

9. Jinmenken Aspect: Your base armour while unarmoured is 1, you gain +10' Speed, and you move on all fours while moving. Creatures have disadvantage on melee attacks while adjacent to you if they can see your face.

10. Visage of Command: You project a 30' persistent zone that forces creatures to make a save, becoming charmed by you for 1 minute on a fail. While charmed in this way, a creature cannot willingly move more than 30' away from you, and you can use the effects of the Command spell against it (non-magically) once per turn as a free action, always using the standard success result. Once a creature has made this save, it is immune to this feature until it takes a long rest.

1. Whisper of Thought: You sense the presence of creatures within 30' of you that are concentrating or casting a spell that can deal psychic damage. You can sense the general direction of the creature.
2. Hushed Clarity: When your Whisper of Thought detects a creature, you also learn whether the creature is hostile, neutral, or friendly to you.
3. Focused Echo: The range of your Whisper of Thought increases to 60'.
4. Mind's Footprint: When your Whisper of Thought detects a creature, you also learn the creature's type.

5. Lingering Trace: You can spend 1 minute concentrating to scan a 30' radius area within your line of sight. The scan reveals whether any creature that would be detected by your Whisper of Thought was present in the area in the past 24 hours, and gives a one-sentence, cryptic impression about the revealed creature with the highest Intelligence.
6. Threading Intuition: You gain an expertise die on insight checks made against creatures detected by your Whisper of Thought.

7. Radiant Ping: Once per long rest, as a free action, you can choose a point within 120' of you. All creatures that can be detected with your Whisper of Thought within 20' of that point are revealed to you: you learn their exact locations and they are rattled until the start of your next turn, and you learn the details of the effect that caused them to be detectable.
8. Deep Resonance: Your Lingering Trace now detects creatures from the past 7 days.

9. Mirrorthread: Once per long rest, when your Whisper of Thought detects a creature, you can form a tenuous link with that creature for 1 minute. While linked, you always know the creature's surface emotion (one word) and you have advantage on Intelligence checks to recall information about that creature or its species.
10. Mindwarden Echo: Your Mirrorthread now lasts for up to 10 minutes and can be used twice between long rests.
1. Luminous Grip: While dual-wielding sword weapons, they shed 5' of dim light and you gain +1 weapon AB.
2. Coordinated Fury: Whenever you take the Attack action while dual-wielding swords, you ignore half and three-quarters cover.

3. Mirrored Parry: Whenever you are targeted by a melee attack while dual-wielding swords, you can reduce the attack's success tier by 1. You can do this a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.
4. Blade Channeling: Once per short rest, when you score a weapon hit while dual-wielding swords, you can recover HP equal to 2d8 + your level.

5. Radiant Riposte: Once per long rest, when an adjacent creature fails to hit you with a melee attack while you are dual-wielding swords, you can use your reaction to make an attack of opportunity against it, dealing 1d8 additional radiant damage.
6. Echoing Blades: Whenever you score a major weapon hit while dual-wielding swords, the target has disadvantage on its next attack before your next turn.
7. Convergent Edge: While dual-wielding swords, your critical damage bonus is doubled.

8. Starforged Momentum: Once per short rest, when you take the Attack action while dual-wielding swords, you can shift up to half your Speed as part of that action. If you hit with the attack, the shift amount increases to your full Speed.

9. Twin Strike: Whenever you take the Attack action while dual-wielding swords, add your main hand weapon's base damage to the attack's damage. This counts as an instance of the Empowered Attack feature.

10. Dual Nova: Your main hand weapon's base damage is doubled for your Radiant Riposte attack, as is the added radiant damage, and the attack is made with advantage. Additionally, the attack deals an additional 6d6 radiant damage and the target is blinded for 1 round on a hit.
1. Slight Stature: If you are Medium or larger, you become Small. If you are already Small, you gain advantage on Stealth checks while in cluttered or domestic environments.

2. Hearth-Home Sense: You can mark one small dwelling (no larger than a 30' cube) as your charge after spending 1 hour inside it. While within that dwelling, you and creatures you designate have +1 armour and whenever any of you would become charmed or frightened, they can make a save, ignoring that condition on a success. The mark lasts until your next long rest, or you mark another location.
3. Clurichaun's Guile: Whenever you successfully hide from a creature within 30' of you and remain hidden from it for 1 further round, you become invisible until the start of your next turn.
4. Clurichaun's Grin: You reduce all journey gold costs by 1.
5. Stolen Shine: You gain an expertise die in Finesse checks.

6. Bottle's Blessing: Whenever you finish a long rest in a city, you gain temporary HP until your next rest equal to a number of d8s equal to your proficiency bonus, and whenever you would become poisoned during that time, you make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
7. Gilded Fingers: You gain a +7 bonus to Finesse checks for pickpocketing (including placing things in pockets).

8. Temper of the Trickster: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you may adopt the temper of the trickster for the remainder of combat. While doing so, you gain advantage on attacks made with simple or improvised weapons, gain a +2 bonus to armour, and the Shove basic maneuver doesn't require you to impose disadvantage on your attack to use it.

9. Faeward Resilience: You gain 50% resistance to poison and psychic damage, and whenever you would be charmed, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success. Additionally, whenever you would be moved against your will while you are in your Hearth-Home Sense dwelling, you can instead teleport up to 15' to an unoccupied space.

10. True Clurichaun: Your Temper of the Trickster now lasts until your next rest, its armour bonus increases to +3, and once per usage of that feature, if you score a major success on an attack you use alongside the Shove basic maneuver, you can force the target to drop one held item of your choice in its space.

1. Keen Claws: You grow retractable, razor-tipped claws on your hands and feet, granting you a natural weapon that deals 1d4 + DEX slashing damage. This natural weapon has the Angled (larger), Deadly, Forceful, Responsive, and Sweep traits.
2. Bristling Hide: While not wearing heavy armour you gain +1 armour and ignore the effects of cold weather on your journey activities.

3. Nose for Blood: You gain advantage on Perception checks that rely on smell and on Survival checks to track creatures by scent. Additionally, you detect the presence of creatures within 30' of you by scent if they are on the ground and do not have full cover from you.
4. Digging Paws: You gain a burrow speed equal to half your Speed and ignore difficult terrain caused by undergrowth, brambles, loose earth, and rubble.
5. Ferocious Resilience: Once per short or long rest, when you are hit, you can reduce the damage by an amount equal to your proficiency bonus + half your level.

6. Wolverine's Frenzy: Whenever you roll for initiative, you can enter a frenzy for the remainder of combat, or until you are knocked unconscious or end the effect as a free action. While frenzied you gain advantage with attacks made with your Keen Claws, they deal 1d6 additional slashing damage, and you lose 1 HP whenever you attack with them. You can enter a frenzy a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.
7. Hardened Resolve: Your Ferocious Resilience's damage reduction increases to double your proficiency bonus + your level. Additionally, while bloodied you gain 50% resistance to physical damage.

8. Predator's Leap: Your jump distance and height are tripled. Once per short or long rest, when you jump at least 10' towards a target, land adjacent to them, and make an attack with your Keen Claws, the attack gains advantage.

9. Adamantine Claws: The base damage die of your Keen Claws increases to a d8, and they gain the Scaling (+1) trait. Additionally, they ignore slashing resistance and immunity. Once per long rest, when you would be reduced to 0 HP, you can instead remain at 1 HP and immediately gain temporary HP equal to your proficiency bonus + your level.

10. Avatar of the Wolverine: While you are not wearing heavy armour, your Strength and Dexterity increase by 2, you gain passive regeneration equal to 1d6 + half your level, you gain immunity to disease, and whenever you would be poisoned or staggered, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
1. Slick Feet: You ignore difficult terrain. Additionally, you ignore any Stealth penalties from moving on noisy surfaces.
2. Easy Step: You can attempt to move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide by making a DC 10 Finesse check.

3. Slip Grip: You can make action escape attempts from grapples and restrains as a bonus action. Additionally, you gain an expertise die on Athletics checks to climb surfaces that are normally slippery.
4. Flowing Motion: Your Slip Grip now allows you to escape grapples and restrains as a free action, and the climbing expertise die it grants increases to a d6.
5. Slidestride: Your Speed increases by 10'. Addiionally, your charged attacks gain +1 AB and deal 1d6 additional force damage.
6. Unsticking: Your Slidestride's Speed bonus increases to 20', and its charged attack damage bonus increases to 2d6.

7. Surface Walk: You can move across vertical surfaces and ceilings as if they were horizontal floors, so long as you move at least 10' along it. You fall if you end your movement on one of these surfaces. Additionally, you reduce incoming bludgeoning harm from falling by 50% and suffer no penalties for falling up to 20'.
8. Slick Mastery: Your Surface Walk no longer requires 10' of movement.

9. Frictionless Step: Whenever you roll for initiative, you can enter a frictionless state for the remainder of combat. In this state, you gain flying speed equal to your Speed but cannot hover, so you must move 10+' on your turn while flying or fall, you gain immunity to the grappled and restrained conditions, and melee attacks made against you have disadvantage. After this effect ends, you gain a level of fatigue until you take a short or long rest.
10. Absolute Slip: Your Frictionless Step now lasts until you take a short or long rest.

1. Hematic Spark: Once per short rest, as a free action, you can form a palm-sized ball of coagulated blood that hovers beside you, which lasts for 1 minute. Whenever you are targeted by a melee attack while the spark is active, you may consume the spark to reduce the attack's success tier by 1.
2. Sticky Mantle: As a free action, you can press your Hematic Spark onto a willing creature, consuming it and granting that creature advantage on its next Stealth check it makes in the next minute.

3. Crimson Lash: As a free action, you can reform your Hematic Spark into a whip-like tendril that lashes at a creature within 30' of you, causing 1d4 necrotic harm and forcing the target to make a save, reducing their Speed by 5' for 1 round on a fail. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus before it consumes your spark.
4. Hardened Shell: Your Hematic Spark default behaviour now reduces an attack's success tier by 2, and can now also apply to ranged attacks.

5. Sanguine Ward: You can expand your Hematic Spark into a sphere of swirling blood that envelops a creature you touch as a free action, consuming the spark. That creature gains temporary HP equal to 1d8 + your proficiency bonus and half cover for 1 minute.
6. Life Tap: Your Crimson Lash's necrotic harm increases to 1d6, and you regain HP equal to half the harm it causes.

7. Hematic Grasp: While a creature is affected by your Sanguine Ward, you can use a free action to have them make a save, becoming restrained by coagulated tendrils on a fail until it passes a passive save. While restrained in this way, a creature suffers 1d4 ongoing necrotic harm and you gain temporary HP equal to the harm caused by this.

8. Blood Mirror: Whenever you would take damage while your Hematic Spark is active or you are within its Sanguine Ward, you can reduce the damage dealtby 1d12, and you gain temporary HP equal to the amount reduced. Every time you use this within a single instance of your spark reduces the die size by 1 (stops functioning after d4).

9. Sanguine Storm: As a free action, you can consume your Hematic Spark to unleash a 20' sphere of blood centred on you. Each foe in that area suffers 1d4 necrotic harm and must make a save, becoming blinded for 1 round on a fail. You regain HP equal to half the necrotic harm caused.

10. Sovereign of Sanguine Flesh: Your Sanguine Storm's necrotic harm increases to 1d6, the radius increases to 30', and after its blinded condition ends on a creature, that creature becomes restrained for a further 1 round.

1. Calm Focus: While you are sober and not under the effect of any behaviour-altering condition, you have advantage on Insight checks and whenever you would be frightened, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.
2. Patient Reserve: Every turn you end having not used either your standard action, bonus action, or moving, you gain a Temperance Charge (maximum 3). All Charges are lost when you take a long rest.
3. Tempered Recovery: Whenever you use hit dice to heal during a short rest, before you roll it, you may expend a Temperance Charge to double the healing received.
4. Steady Gains: Your maximum Temperance Charges increases to 5.

5. Measured Defence: Whenever you are targeted by an attack, you can expend a Temperance Charge to reduce its success tier by 1. You can expend Charges this way a number of times between long rests equal to your proficiency bonus.

6. Quiet Clarity: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative, you can enter a quiet state for the remainder of combat. In this state, you cannot lose concentration against your will and whenever you would be charmed or frightened, make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.

7. Tempered Strike: Whenever you make a damaging attack, you can expend a Temperance Charge to add 1d8 psychic damage to its damage, and on a hit, the arget gets disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn. You can expend Charges in this way a number of times between long rests equal to half your proficiency bonus.

8. Serene Bastion: Whenever you would be reduced to 0 HP, you can expend up to 3 Temperance Charges to remaing at 1 HP and grant temporary HP to you and allies within 10' equal to the number of Charges spent times 6. Additionally, whenever an affected creature would be frightened in the next round, they make a save, ignoring the condition on a success.

9. Temperance Mastery: Your maximum Temperance Charges increases to 7, and whenever you expend any, you may choose one of the following additional benefits to occur at the same time: regain 6 HP; reduce the next attack roll against you by 1d4; or if you are currently affected by your Quiet Clarity, you can extend its duration until your next rest.

10. Equilibrium Exemplar: Once per long rest, when you roll for initiative with 3+ Temperance Charges, you can expend 3 Charges to assume Equilibrium for the remainder of combat. While doing so, you gain immunity to the charmed and frightened conditions, gain 50% resistance to all damage, and whenever you hit with an attack, you recover HP equal to 1d12 + your level + your proficiency bonus.
1. Sticky Step: Whenever you leave a space, you can leave faint adhesive in it. The next time a foe enters that space, it becomes sluggish for 1 round.
2. Trailing Snag: Whenever you score a melee hit or push a creature, you gain advantage on the first opportunity attack you make against it before the end of your next turn.

3. Pulling Thread: Whenever a creature within 30' of you begins to move, you can force it to make a save. On a fail, you reduce its relevant speed by up to 15' and after it finishes moving may shift up to half that reduced distance towards the creature.
4. Tether: Instead of shifting towards a creature with your Pulling Thread, you can instead push the creature 10'.

5. Webbed Ground: Once per short or long rest as a free action, you can creature a 15' radius area of difficult terrain centred on a point within 60' for 1 minute. Creatures you designate ignore this difficult terrain.
6. Snare: Your Webbed Ground is now a persistent zone that forces affected creatures to make a save, becoming restrained for 1 round on a fail and sluggish for 1 round on a success.

7. Iron Lattice: As a free action, you can weave an iron lattice across a 30' cone, requiring your concentration and lasting for up to 1 minute. The lattice is a persistent zone that causes 1d4 slashing harm to foes and forces them to make a save, becoming restrained on a fail and sluggish on a success, both until passive save. As a free action on each of your turns while maintaining the lattice, you can move the lattice up to 15' in any direction.
